bullets.text: Underwriting profit margin 6.6%, exceeding 4.0% goal; core margin 6.9%; net income $400.0M ($5.31/share); operating income $336.0M ($4.46/share); ROE 20.9% vs 20.5% in 1996; underwriting profit posted for 25th time in 31 years.

Total shareholder return was 78.4%, ranking 28th in S&P 500; Midland Financial acquired for about $50 million; capital prioritized to support underwriting without issuing stock; optimal capital structure believed to maintain 'A' ratings.
NPW +36% to $4,665.1M vs $3,441.7M in 1996; core business NPW grew 33% to $4,467.4M, representing 96% of total volume; standard and preferred auto accounted for 20% to 25% of core.

30,000+ independent agencies sell products; agencies writing standard and preferred auto more than doubled, driving 126% growth in agent-produced standard/preferred new policies; phone channel 1-800-AUTO-PRO quotes competitor rates.

Consumer financial responsibility rating was approved and used in 31 states representing 80% of core written premiums; countrywide auto rates lowered an average 0.9%; company continues learning standard and preferred pricing.

Underwriting expense ratio was 22.5% vs 21.6% in 1996 (35.0% in 1990); Gainsharing represented 14.4% of total compensation; payout exceeding the annual target had a 0.5 point effect on the expense ratio.
Total auto policyholders increased by 575,000 to 2.5 million; answered 16 million telephone calls 24/7; daily claims call volume reached 25,000, supported by new phone switches and workflows.

First auto insurer conducting direct Internet sales and online payments in 1997 after launching site in 1995; deployed Ownership Workbench for servicing and wireless Claims Workbench for off-site representatives.

Expanded consumer advertising into over 40 media markets across 19 states, adding 13 states in 1997; situational campaigns dramatize consumer concerns regarding claims and buying experiences with auto insurance.

Industry P&C net premiums written to surplus ratio reached 0.9-to-1, lowest in 60 years; monitored regulatory changes including California's Proposition 213 and Louisiana's mandatory 10% rate rollback law.
